result.title: Task-Utility IQA: Rethinking Image Quality Assessment in Embodied Tasks
result.summary: Image quality assessment (IQA) underpins embodied imaging pipelines by judging whether visual quality satisfies downstream tasks, yet most existing methods learn task-agnostic scores aligned with generic human ratings on static benchmarks. This objective mismatches embodied and interactive settings, where image adequacy depends on task goals, context, and action requirements that shape an agent's decisions. We argue that IQA should shift from score regression to goal-conditioned judgment defined by embodied task utility. To this end, we propose an MLLM-based embodied IQA agent framework that reasons about task requirements, grounds quality evidence, and produces decision-facing assessments. A compact VisDrone evidence study shows that conventional perceptual metrics and generic MLLM-based IQA scores are weak proxies for downstream VLM task success, while a task-conditioned utility score better predicts whether visual input supports the target task. These findings support a task-utility-oriented reframing of IQA for embodied, explainable, and decision-aware visual perception.

AI.brief_summary: 论文主张图像质量评估应从通用人类评分的分数回归，转向以具身任务效用为条件的目标导向判断，并提出基于 MLLM 的 IQA agent 框架：推理任务需求、定位质量证据、输出面向决策的评估；小规模 VisDrone 实验显示传统感知指标与通用 IQA 分数难以预测下游 VLM 任务成功，而任务条件化效用分数预测更好。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「视觉输入是否足以支撑目标任务」的任务效用判据与 LVR 中任务必要视觉信息能否被获取、证据筛选与停止判断相关，可供核查；但该工作面向输入质量评价而非 latent 状态生成，效用分数与下游推理成败的因果作用仍需进一步验证。
